question.text:
Consider the partition of the rectangular region $R$ shown above and the positive function $f(x,y)$ defined on $R.$ Which of the following gives an expression for the upper Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to this partition.

Hint: $M_{ij}$ denotes the maximum value of $f$ on the subregion $R_{ij}$
question.explanation:
To calculate the upper Riemann sum $U$ with respect to the given partition, we compute the sum of the volumes of $3$ rectangular solids, one for each $R_{ij}.$

The volume of the rectangular solid corresponding to each subregion $R_{ij}$ is given by

\[ M_{ij}\cdot \textrm{Area}(R_{ij}). \]

where $M_{ij}$ denotes the maximum value of $f$ on the subregion $R_{ij}.$ We pick the maximum value of $f$ because we're finding the upper sum.

So in our case, we have

\[ U = M_{11}\cdot \textrm{Area}(R_{11}) + M_{12}\cdot \textrm{Area}(R_{12}) + M_{13}\cdot \textrm{Area}(R_{13}). \]

Notice that

\[ \textrm{Area}(R_{11}) = \textrm{Area}(R_{12}) = \textrm{Area}(R_{13}) = 2. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} U &= 2\cdot M_{11} + 2\cdot M_{12} + 2\cdot M_{13}\\[3pt] &= 2(M_{11}+M_{12}+M_{13}). \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating an Upper Riemann Sum in the Case of a Strictly Decreasing Function

question.text:
Let $R = [1,4] \times [2,4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y) = 16-xy.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

\begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{1,2,3,4\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{2,4\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$
question.explanation:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

\[ U(f,P) = M_{11}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{11}) + M_{21}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{21}) + M_{31}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{31}), \]

where $M_{ij}$ is the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$ We pick the maximum value of $f$ because we're finding the upper sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\textrm{Area}(R_{ij}) = 2$ for all $3$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

\begin{align*} U(f,P) &= 2\cdot M_{11} + 2\cdot M_{21} + 2\cdot M_{31} \\ &= 2(M_{11} + M_{21} + M_{31}). \end{align*}

Now, notice that

  • $f(x,y) = 16-xy$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = 16-xy$ decreases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible $x$ and the smallest possible $y.$ This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

Hence:

\[ \begin{align*} M_{11} &= f\left(1,2\right) = 14 \\[5pt] M_{21} &= f\left(2,2\right) = 12 \\[5pt] M_{31} &= f\left(3,2\right) = 10 \end{align*} \]

Finally,

\begin{align*} U(f,P) &= 2(14+12+10) \\[3pt] &= 72. \end{align*}

\[ U(f,P) = M_{11}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{11}) + M_{21}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{21}) + M_{12}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{12}) + M_{22}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{22}), \]

where $M_{ij}$ is the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$ We pick the maximum value of $f$ because we're finding the upper sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\textrm{Area}(R_{ij}) = 1$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

\[ U(f,P) = M_{11} + M_{21} + M_{31} + M_{41}. \]

Now, notice that

  • $f(x,y) = 10-4x-2y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = 10-4x-2y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible $x$ and the smallest possible $y.$ This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

\[ U(f,P) = M_{11}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{11}) + M_{21}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{21}) + M_{12}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{12}) + M_{22}\cdot\textrm{Area}(R_{22}), \]

where $M_{ij}$ is the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$ We pick the maximum value of $f$ because we're finding the upper sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\textrm{Area}(R_{ij}) = 8$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to \begin{align} U(f,P) &= 8\cdot M_{11} + 8\cdot M_{21}+ 8\cdot M_{12} + 8\cdot M_{22} \\ &= 8(M_{11} + M_{21}+ M_{12} + M_{22}). \end{align}

Now, notice that

  • $f(x,y) = x+y$ increases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = x+y$ increases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible $x$ and the largest possible $y.$ This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

Hence:

\begin{align*} M_{11} &= f\left(6,5\right) = 11 \\[5pt] M_{21} &= f\left(10,5\right) = 15 \\[5pt] M_{12} &= f\left(6,7\right) = 13 \\[5pt] M_{22} &= f\left(10,7\right) = 17 \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} U(f,P) &=8(11+15+13+17)\\[3pt] &=448. \end{align*}
